stories.title: $174M Sale Closes for 783K-SF Frederickson Industrial Facility
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has arranged the sale of a 782,775 square-foot industrial facility located in Frederickson, Washington. The property is fully leased to Harbor Freight Tools and has an average weighted lease term of 8.8 years, making it a core investment opportunity in the Seattle-Tacoma industrial market. The Cushman & Wakefield team of Bryce Aberg, Jeff Chiate, Matthew Leupold, Charlie Jacobs and Jeffrey Cole represented the seller in the transaction. The property was acquired by an institutional industrial investor. “This transaction shines a light on the continued demand for institutional-quality logistics assets in core Pacific Northwest locations,” said Aberg. “The disposition of Fred 310 Harbor Freight demonstrates the ongoing flight to quality, driving the greater Pacific Northwest industrial markets.” The property comprises a single industrial building featuring modern warehouse and distribution specifications. Designed for large-scale logistics operations, the building includes high clear heights, ample dock-high loading positions and expansive truck courts. FRED310 Industrial Park was developed by Panattoni and Crow Holdings Capital. Connect Industrial West | August 20 | Irvine, CAOn August 20, Connect Industrial West will bring together the owners, investors, developers, brokers, lenders, and occupiers driving industrial real estate across the Western U.S. Join top decision-makers for an afternoon of market insights, dealmaking opportunities, and networking with the industry’s most influential players.  Register now: www.connectindustrialwest2026.com The post $174M Sale Closes for 783K-SF Frederickson Industrial Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cushman & Wakefield closed $174M sale of 783K-SF Harbor Freight facility in Frederickson, WA
8.8-year weighted lease term sold to institutional industrial investor; demonstrates flight-to-quality trend

stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield arranged the $174 million sale of a fully leased 782,775-square-foot industrial facility in Frederickson, Washington, anchored by Harbor Freight Tools with an 8.8-year average lease term. An institutional industrial investor purchased the asset from the seller. The transaction underscores continued demand for institutional-quality logistics properties in core Pacific Northwest submarkets, driven by a broader institutional flight to quality.
stories.impact: Seattle-Tacoma industrial market remains a magnet for institutional capital seeking long-lease, modern logistics assets. This validates the supply-chain infrastructure thesis in the Pacific Northwest and suggests continued rent resilience in these core nodes, making development-ready land in West/North Seattle and Tacoma suburbs attractive for multifamily infill near employment clusters.

stories.title: Global Healthcare REIT Acquires EmblemHealth-Leased Brooklyn MOB
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged the $89-million sale of Emblem Health Hub Medical Office Building, a 140,000-square-foot, trophy-quality MOB located at 101 Pennsylvania Ave. in Brooklyn’s East New York neighborhood. Vital Infrastructure Property Trust, a Canada-based global healthcare infrastructure REIT, acquired the property from developer Dominion Management Company. Co-Heads of U.S. Medical Office Capital Markets Ben Appel, U.S. Capital Markets Adam Spies, U.S. Healthcare Capital Markets Jay Miele and Justin Shepherd, alongside Head of Healthcare Debt John Nero, Executive Vice Chairman Adam Doneger, Vice Chairman Matt Berres, Senior Managing Director Michael Greeley and Associate Directors Ron Ott, Conor Hilton and Drew Martin, represented the seller. Completed as one of Brooklyn’s newest purpose-built medical office developments, Emblem Health Hub is fully leased long-term to EmblemHealth, New York’s largest independent physician group. “Institutional investors globally continue to prioritize high-quality medical office assets backed by strong healthcare operators, drawing investor interest from the U.S, Canada, Middle East, UK, and Asia,” said Appel. The post Global Healthcare REIT Acquires EmblemHealth-Leased Brooklyn MOB appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Vital Infrastructure Property Trust (Canada REIT) acquired $89M Brooklyn medical office building fully leased to EmblemHealth

stories.summary: Newmark arranged the $89 million sale of Emblem Health Hub, a 140,000-square-foot medical office building in Brooklyn's East New York neighborhood, to Vital Infrastructure Property Trust, a Canada-based healthcare REIT. The property is fully leased long-term to EmblemHealth, New York's largest independent physician group. The transaction signals strong global institutional appetite for high-quality, healthcare-operator-backed medical office assets.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact, but signals physician-group expansion and healthcare infrastructure investment in outer Brooklyn (East New York) submarkets. Worth monitoring: if EmblemHealth's growth continues, associated downstream demand for workforce housing near this medical hub and along the transport corridors connecting to Manhattan could support residential development in adjacent East Brooklyn and Canarsie areas.

stories.title: Cabot Properties Sells 2.5M-SF Midwest Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Cabot Properties, a global investor, developer, and operator of logistics properties, today announced the successful disposition of the North Central Portfolio, a collection of 11 modern industrial properties totaling approximately 2.5 million square feet across key industrial submarkets in Greater Chicago and Minneapolis, Minnesota. The diversified portfolio, which includes assets both developed and acquired by Cabot, was purchased by a prominent global asset manager. The Chicago-based CBRE Capital Markets team represented Cabot in the transactions. Six of the properties are located in the North/Central Kane County and West Suburbs submarkets of the Greater Chicago area and include four cross-dock facilities and two rear-load properties, totaling approximately 1.6 million square feet. The buildings are 97% occupied by a variety of tenants across various logistics and distribution uses. The additional five buildings comprise approximately one million square feet across Minneapolis’ Northwest and Southwest submarkets. The properties are 100% leased to a variety of distribution and light manufacturing occupiers. From shifting capital flows and debt trends to evolving occupier demand and development strategies, take part in the conversations shaping the future of industrial real estate. stories.summary: Cabot Properties divested the North Central Portfolio, comprising 11 modern industrial properties totaling 2.5 million square feet across Greater Chicago and Minneapolis-St. Paul. Six Chicago-area properties (1.6M SF) in North/Central Kane County and West Suburbs are 97% occupied by logistics and distribution tenants; five Minneapolis properties (1M SF) are 100% leased to distribution and light manufacturing operators. A prominent global asset manager purchased the entire portfolio via CBRE Capital Markets.
stories.impact: Chicago West Suburbs and Minneapolis Northwest/Southwest submarkets remain institutional-grade logistics hubs with strong fundamentals (97–100% occupancy) attracting global capital. Strong absorption and leasing velocity in these markets signal sustained supply-chain demand; multifamily developers should prioritize mixed-use projects near these logistics corridors, especially in Chicago's West Suburbs and West Loop, and Minneapolis's North Loop, where live-work proximity appeals to younger logistics and supply-chain workforce.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Sale of Grocery-Anchored Shopping Center in Virginia
stories.excerpt: CBRE has arranged the sale of 5th Street Station, a 451,779-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center in Charlottesville. Bridge33 Capital LLC purchased the property from S.J. Collins Enterprises for an undisclosed amount. Chris Munley, Colin Behr, Ryan Sciullo, and Casey Smith of CBRE’s National Retail Partners team represented the seller in the transaction. “We are excited to enter Virginia with this dominant property in the growing market of Charlottesville,” said Peter Trahanas, Director of Investments at Bridge33 Capital. “This acquisition will add the second Wegmans and the first Dick’s House of Sport to our portfolio. We look forward to creating lasting value at the center and being a part of the Charlottesville community.” Located just off Interstate 64 at 5th Street Station Parkway, the property is in close proximity to the University of Virginia. The property is anchored by Wegmans and features a mix of national, regional and local retailers, including Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, Dick’s House of Sport, PetSmart, Panera Bread and Jersey Mike’s. The post CBRE Arranges Sale of Grocery-Anchored Shopping Center in Virginia appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: CBRE arranged the sale of 5th Street Station, a 451,779-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center in Charlottesville, Virginia, to Bridge33 Capital LLC. The property, located off Interstate 64 near the University of Virginia, is anchored by Wegmans and features a diverse tenant mix including Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, Dick's House of Sport, and national retailers. The acquisition marks Bridge33's entry into the Virginia market.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, Charlottesville's proximity to UVA, growing retail stabilization, and I-64 accessibility suggest improving labor-force demographics and spending power in the submarket. Worth tracking for future mixed-use development (student + young professional housing) near campus and downtown; retail lease velocity signals durable local demand.

stories.title: Declining Empire State Building Visits Drive Q2 Loss for ESRT
stories.excerpt: New York City’s declines in international tourism over the past year since President Donald Trump assumed office are starting to affect Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT)’s finances. The real estate investment trust (REIT) reported second-quarter funds from operations (FFO) of $57 million, or 21 cents per share, marking a loss of $25.8 million or 15 cents per share from the same period a year ago. ESRT attributed the loss largely to a “massive” non-cash impairment charge of $166.11 million connected to underperforming visitations in the Empire State Building observatory stemming from persistent drops in international tourists to the Big Apple. The observatory generated $12.4 million of net income in the first quarter, a sharp 48.5 percent decrease from $24.1 million in the same period in 2025. Visitors to the observatory during the quarter were 450,000, down 28.5 percent year-over-year. In addition to the decline of international visitors to the U.S., ESRT also attributed the profit loss to lower usage of third-party pass program channels used for tourist sites around New York. Such passes are often used by budget-conscious international travelers. “While all attractions have experienced reduced visitorship in 2026, our drop compared to the market in general is larger due to our prior dominance with pass programs and their international presence,” Anthony Malkin, CEO of ESRT, said during the firm’s earnings call early Thursday afternoon. “Softer visitation persisted through the second quarter.” Projections for reduced visits to the observatory prompted ESRT to reduce its 2026 core FFO assumptions to a range of 75 cents to 79 cents per share compared to 85 cents to 89 cents per share FFO in February. Malkin said the Empire State Building has in the past seen more than 60 percent of its observatory traffic derive from international travelers, but that number shifted to 40 percent last week when it performed its second highest visitor numbers of 2026. Observatory visitation fell 28.5% year-over-year to 450,000 visitors, and net observatory income plummeted 48.5% in Q1 2026 compared to Q1 2025. ESRT attributed the collapse to persistent declines in international tourist arrivals to New York City.
stories.impact: Signals major headwind to Manhattan office-to-residential conversion fundamentals. International tourism and business-travel declines reduce net migration, spending, and daytime population density in Midtown, pressuring Office conversion economics and rental-demand growth. Multifamily developers should deprioritize Midtown office conversion deals and favor outer-borough, transit-connected residential projects in neighborhoods with strong local job growth (Life Sciences, tech, healthcare) independent of tourist/international business cycles.

stories.title: Blackstone Mortgage Trust Posts Q2 Net Loss Amid Focus on Portfolio Diversification
stories.excerpt: Blackstone Mortgage Trust (BXMT) reported a net loss of $81.2 million in the second quarter of 2026, but its executives were optimistic during a Thursday morning earnings call about turning its portfolio around. The publicly traded mortgage real estate investment trust (REIT) posted a second-quarter loss of 48 cents per share with a distributable earnings per share of 48 cents, still beating analysts’ estimates of 38 cents per share. BXMT executives attributed the drop in earnings to short-term impacts from several loan impairments during the second quarter, specifically the resolution of a $29 million impaired multifamily loan in Dallas. “It’s hard given all the moving pieces right now, and it’s still early in the quarter. Obviously, given some of the impairments we took in Q2 and the pretty substantial repayment volume that we had this quarter, we do expect some impact to the third quarter,” Marcin Urbaszek, chief financial officer at BXMT and managing director at Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies, said during the call. “But, again, it’ll take us probably a couple quarters to be fully deployed with the money that we’re getting back,” Urbaszek added. “It’s hard to say exactly where we’re going to be right now on a runway basis. stories.summary: Blackstone Mortgage Trust reported a $81.2 million net loss in Q2 2026 (−48 cents per share) but posted distributable earnings per share of 48 cents, beating analyst estimates of 38 cents. The loss stemmed from loan impairments, notably a $29 million multifamily loan resolution in Dallas, and substantial repayment volumes during the quarter. Executives remain optimistic about portfolio diversification and turning around performance in the coming quarters.
stories.impact: Dallas multifamily loan impairment signals stress in specific submarkets or sponsor quality tiers; BXMT's selective write-downs and pivot away from troubled assets suggest disciplined underwriting but also tightening of leverage available to second-tier sponsors. Multifamily developers should expect continued lending caution in overbuilt markets (Dallas, Austin) and higher rates/equity requirements for non-core sponsors; strong balance sheets and proven track records will command better capital access.

stories.title: CRE Loan Delinquencies Decline in Q2; CMBS Remains Elevated
stories.excerpt: Delinquency rates for mortgages backed by commercial properties decreased during the second quarter of 2026. That’s according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) latest commercial real estate finance (CREF) Loan Performance Survey, which reported that CMBS delinquencies declined during Q2 but remain elevated relative to other lender types. The survey found that the share of loans that were delinquent generally declined across the major property types, though performance remained mixed. Office and lodging continued to exhibit the highest delinquency rates. CMBS delinquencies fell by 39 basis points to 4.82% during the quarter. The second-highest delinquency rate was for life company loans, which also saw an improvement during Q2, falling 28 bps to 1.19%. “Commercial mortgage loan performance improved during the second quarter, with delinquency rates declining across most major property types and capital sources,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial real estate research. “While office and lodging properties continue to face challenges and CMBS delinquency rates remain elevated relative to other lenders, the overall decline in non-current loan balances points to continued stability in the commercial mortgage market.” The post CRE Loan Delinquencies Decline in Q2; CMBS Remains Elevated appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MBA Commercial Real Estate Finance Survey: Q2 CMBS delinquencies fell 39 bps to 4.82%; all major asset types improved

stories.summary: The Mortgage Bankers Association's CREF Loan Performance Survey reported that CMBS delinquencies declined 39 basis points to 4.82% in Q2 2026, though they remain elevated relative to life company loans (1.19%). Delinquency rates generally improved across major property types, though office and lodging continued to exhibit the highest delinquency rates. The overall decline in non-current loan balances signals continued stability in CRE mortgages.
stories.impact: Improving CMBS and life-company loan performance outside office/lodging removes systemic financing stress, improving capital availability and pricing for multifamily acquisition and development debt. Strong multifamily fundamentals (not mentioned in delinquency discussions) position residential debt as flight-to-quality asset class. Multifamily developers should expect favorable debt terms and lower rates relative to struggling property types; this is a window to lock in low-cost leverage before multifamily cap rates compress further.

stories.title: Vici Properties Is Standing By to Build a Las Vegas NBA Arena
stories.excerpt: Vici Properties executives during a Thursday morning earnings call teased the possibility of building a National Basketball Association (NBA) arena complex on land the company owns in Las Vegas. In addition to being the largest owner on the Las Vegas Strip with properties including the Venetian, Mandalay Bay, the MGM Grand and Caesars Palace, the Manhattan-based Vici also controls several dozen undeveloped acres behind the Planet Hollywood, Paris and Horseshoe casinos. The NBA toward the start of 2026 began formally reviewing the possibility of adding a Las Vegas franchise. The move highlighted what Vici President and Chief Operating Officer John Payne noted on the earnings call was the “massive growth in pro sports” in Las Vegas. Major League Baseball’s Oakland A’s are relocating to Las Vegas, and the city in the past 10 years has added National Football League, National Hockey League and Women’s National Basketball Association teams. Nothing is finalized regarding developing an NBA arena complex, despite weeks of media speculation. Executives on the second-quarter earnings call did not discuss any moves in depth. The addition of such a complex, though, would fit into the strategy of a company that bills itself as an “experiential real estate investment trust.” Its 103-property portfolio inside and outside of Las Vegas is capitalizing on a particularly robust era for experiential retail. The market for experiential retail globally is expected to more than quadruple from the $132 billion it stood at toward the start of 2026, according to market research firm Metatech Insights. Heck, one of the fastest-growing commercial real estate asset classes in the U.S. and Canada is trampoline parks. (Ed Pitoniak, Vici’s CEO, told Commercial Observer in April 2025 that when he mastered the experiential retail approach, “I tell people I died and went to business heaven.”) Vici’s second-quarter numbers reflected the boom times. stories.summary: Vici Properties executives teased the possibility of building an NBA arena complex on undeveloped land the company owns in Las Vegas. Vici controls several dozen acres behind the Planet Hollywood, Paris, and Horseshoe casinos. The move would capitalize on the NBA's formal 2026 review of Las Vegas expansion, following recent relocations of the Oakland A's to Vegas and the city's addition of NFL, NHL, and WNBA franchises over the past decade.
stories.impact: Major indirect demand signal for Las Vegas multifamily. An NBA franchise + arena would accelerate population inflow, job growth (hospitality, service, construction), and corporate relocation to Las Vegas, strengthening rental demand across submarkets. Multifamily developers should aggressively acquire or entitle land in central/west Las Vegas, Downtown, and transit corridors near the Strip; peak rent growth likely 2–3 years post-arena opening as population influx compounds with hospitality wage growth.

stories.title: Mezcali Founders to Open New Fusion Concept in Financial District
stories.excerpt: The restaurateurs behind Mexican restaurant Mezcali and American tavern the Malt House have signed a lease for a new food concept in Manhattan’s Financial District. Eoin Foyle and Darren Shore signed a 20-year, 4,744-square-foot lease in the retail component of TF Cornerstone’s 2 Gold Street, where they will launch their latest brainchild, a Hawaiian-Caribbean-Asian fusion restaurant called Solerum, according to the landlord. TF Cornerstone did not immediately disclose the asking rent for the space, but the average retail asking rent for retail space on the nearby corridor of Broadway from Battery Park to Chambers Street was $224 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “As the Financial District continues to evolve into one of New York City’s most dynamic mixed-use neighborhoods, we’re committed to curating a retail experience that enhances the everyday lives of our residents, while serving the broader community,” Steve Gonzalez, vice president of retail leasing at TF Cornerstone, said in a statement. “Solerum’s distinctive concept and hospitality-driven dining experience make it an excellent addition to the neighborhood.” Manu Wendum and John DiGangi of Retail by MONA negotiated on behalf of the tenant, while Steven Baker, Daniyel Cohen and Tom Galo of RTL Partners represented TF Cornerstone in the deal. Retail by MONA and Baker did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “The opening of Solerum at 2 Gold Street represents our continued investment in New York City and the Financial District, a neighborhood that has played an important role in the growth of our restaurant business,” Foyle said in a statement. 2 Gold Street sits between Maiden Lane and Platt Street, across the street from Mezcali at 83 Maiden Lane and three blocks from the Malt House at 9 Maiden Lane. The Malt House also has a location at 206 Thompson Street in Greenwich Village. The Gold Street pro
bullets: Mezcali/Malt House restaurateurs signed 20-year lease for new Solerum fusion restaurant at TF Cornerstone's 2 Gold Street, Financial District

stories.summary: Restaurateurs Eoin Foyle and Darren Shore signed a 20-year, 4,744-square-foot lease for Solerum, a Hawaiian-Caribbean-Asian fusion concept, in TF Cornerstone's 2 Gold Street in Manhattan's Financial District. The property is part of a mixed-use development. Comparable Broadway corridor retail (Battery Park to Chambers Street) was asking $224 per square foot in Q2 2026. TF Cornerstone emphasized its strategy to curate retail experiences supporting the neighborhood's evolution into a dynamic mixed-use destination.
stories.impact: Financial District retail activation (premium independent dining, long-term leases) signals sustained residential occupancy demand and landlord confidence in daytime/evening population recovery. Retail uptick in lower Manhattan suggests successful mixed-use densification and reduced office-conversion risk in core Financial District; multifamily operators and developers should prioritize ground-floor retail activation and expect stronger rent growth in Financial District and Tribeca as mixed-use synergies strengthen post-pandemic.

stories.title: Hudson Investing Secures $52M Acquisition Debt, Equity for Indianapolis Asset
stories.excerpt: Hudson Investing has secured $52.1 million in acquisition financing for Maple Knoll Apartments, a 300-unit garden-style multifamily complex just outside Indianapolis, Ind., Commercial Observer can first report. Torchlight Investment provided the equity, while Northmarq structured the full capital stack for the transaction, providing the senior debt directly through Northmarq’s in-house Freddie Mac platform. A Northmarq team of Annamarie Bjorklund and Cody Field arranged the transaction. Bjorklund said in a statement that Northmarq was able to secure both the debt and equity from Torchlight due to Hudson’s reputation as “a disciplined, well-capitalized sponsor.” “We knew as soon as we met the Hudson team and saw their plan for the asset that they would be a natural fit,” Bjorklund said. “Ultimately, Torchlight stood out, and we’re excited for their new partnership and to see the next chapter for a great property.” Located at 500 Bigleaf Maple Way in Westfield, a city 20 miles north of Downtown Indianapolis, Maple Knoll Apartments opened in 2007 and features 18 three-story apartment buildings across 24 acres, all of which contain one- to three-bedroom units. Hudson Investing is purchasing the property from Marquette Companies and HIMCO, but previous owners include Blackstone and GE Capital. The acquisition is part of Hudson’s value-add strategy, and the firm plans to invest capital to renovate the entire property, according to a release from Northmarq. “We continue to see Indianapolis as a highly attractive investment market with strong population growth, quality employment drivers and desirable suburban communities that continue to attract residents,” said Kent Ritter, CEO of Hudson Investing. bullets: Hudson Investing secured $52.1M acquisition financing for Maple Knoll Apartments (300-unit garden-style) in Westfield, IN (20 miles north of Indianapolis)

stories.summary: Hudson Investing secured $52.1 million in acquisition financing for Maple Knoll Apartments, a 300-unit garden-style multifamily complex in Westfield, Indiana, approximately 20 miles north of downtown Indianapolis. Torchlight Investment provided equity, while Northmarq structured the full capital stack using its in-house Freddie Mac platform for senior debt. Northmarq highlighted Hudson's reputation as a disciplined, well-capitalized sponsor in securing both debt and equity from Torchlight.
stories.impact: Indianapolis suburban market (Westfield submarket) shows strong capital availability and sponsor-reputation arbitrage. Freddie Mac platform ease and Torchlight willingness to pair with Hudson signals investor confidence in suburban Indianapolis multifamily fundamentals and stable value-add opportunities. Developers should pursue acquisition and light-value-add deals in Indianapolis suburbs; lower cost basis and strong lending support vs. coastal markets create favorable return profiles for 2026–2027.
